scientific_question: Within each dataset, do independently calibrated Nominal and PESS policies choose pairwise-MCV extstats sets with different PostgreSQL cardinality-estimation generalization on a prospectively frozen query cohort that was not used for resource selection? Empty is a matched baseline.

calibration_and_selection.calibration_source: within-dataset development/calibration queries only; query structures and labels available to calibration are frozen and hashed before selection
calibration_and_selection.calibration_sample_policy: Use only the predeclared physical sample replicate 0 for validation calibration and resource selection. For each of the 1000 calibration queries, record Empty and each candidate singleton estimate once on the same replicate-0 sample block; derive the frozen corrected-log coefficients and select resource sets. Replicate 1 is never used for calibration/selection and is reserved for out-of-sample sample-sensitivity evaluation. Both sample blocks evaluate the same held-out cohort.
calibration_and_selection.test_firewall: selection code receives candidate universe, validation calibration records and budgets only; it must not receive test SQL literals, test truth, test estimates, PostgreSQL test traces, or post-selection feedback
calibration_and_selection.model: use the corrected natural-log definitions and Nominal/PESS objectives from a separately reviewed, hash-pinned implementation; the PR #58 validation-only source pin above is a reference, not authorization to execute its historical runner; never use defective formal-v4 coefficients
calibration_and_selection.nominal_scheme: deterministic greedy maximal matching in frozen candidate order, as a scoped mathematical policy definition only
calibration_and_selection.pess_scheme: all maximal matchings of the selected task graph; maximal is not maximum-cardinality; task-wise worst loss remains the frozen PESS objective
calibration_and_selection.loss: positive pre-clamp absolute natural-log error under the reviewed frozen model; optimizer objective is not the held-out evaluation metric

resource_budget.meaning: unit-count budget: one unit per selected statistics object; this is a candidate-count proxy, not a measured/proxy-weighted physical Maint or ANALYZE-time budget
resource_budget.infeasible: report INFEASIBLE; never substitute a neighboring budget

ties.optimization: enumerate/report every objective-optimal unordered resource set
ties.deployed_set: lexicographically smallest sorted tuple of candidate IDs among optimal sets; records all tied alternatives
ties.pg_creation_order: ascending frozen candidate index, separately recorded; does not redefine the unordered optimizer decision

cohort_generation_recipe.source_pin: base source tree a89c1a70d96abc346f988860661e7f1a9f6297b5 plus verified Issue #59 dataset specifications and source archive SHA256 5cd33cba7f3d7182ef497e60e7346fb2a7546941590a90a4444913a944958f79; execution manifest must pin prepared CSV/schema bytes, row-order hash, dataset-spec source hash and exact Python/libmpdec versions
cohort_generation_recipe.prng: counter_u64 = first 8 SHA256 bytes, big-endian, of UTF-8 'ess-stage2b-cohort-v1\0{dataset}\0{seed}\0{attempt}\0{purpose}\0{retry}'. randbelow(n) uses rejection sampling with limit=2^64-(2^64 mod n), retrying with retry+1 when word>=limit. All choices use distinct fixed purpose strings; column subsets are the first d columns after sorting by (counter_u64 purpose=column-rank, stable column ID).
cohort_generation_recipe.template_draw: For each attempt, draw d uniformly from 1..D; choose d distinct columns by sorting the hash-counter draw keyed by stable column ID and taking the first d. For each selected column, use its pinned DatasetSpec type: categorical columns get '=', numeric columns choose uniformly from '=', '<', '<=', '>', '>=', '[]'. Predicate list is sorted by stable source-column UTF-8 bytes before serialization and SQL rendering. Reject duplicate template SHA, unsupported schema/operator, and any template in the historical fingerprint quarantine.
cohort_generation_recipe.literal_draw: For each attempt draw one deterministic source-table row ordinal using randbelow(row_count,purpose='source-row-ordinal'). With probability 0.9 use the row's selected-column values as a joint in-domain center; with probability 0.1 independently draw each selected-column value from its observed domain (categorical: uniform over sorted distinct values; numeric/date: uniform over the closed min/max domain after schema-typed conversion; OOD in the AreCEL sense of independent centers, not necessarily outside marginal domains). Equality and one-sided inequalities use the center as their literal. For '[]', draw width with equal probability from uniform[0, domain-span] or exponential(lambda=10/domain-span), using u=(1+randbelow(2^53-1,...))/2^53, Decimal precision 80, Decimal.ln/exp; center the interval on the selected value and convert endpoints using the pinned schema type/renderer. Render typed literals using the pinned AreCEL source renderer. Pin CSV parser, source CSV SHA, row-order SHA and observed per-column domains in the manifest. This is AreCEL-inspired workload generation, not a reproduction of learned-estimator training.

fingerprint_contract.template: byte-for-byte reuse Issue #59 audit_structure.py::normalised_template: sorted (column, operator, 'range' iff operator=='[]' else 'scalar') tuples, json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False,separators=(',',':')), then SHA256 UTF-8
fingerprint_contract.exact: byte-for-byte reuse Issue #59 audit_structure.py::canonical_predicate_fingerprint: ordered [column,operator,value] tuples in canonical SQL predicate order, compact UTF-8 JSON ensure_ascii=False allow_nan=False, then SHA256
fingerprint_contract.query_group: one normalized template SHA is one group and has exactly one generated SQL/query ID; no group contributes more than one observation to any statistic

cohort_generation_recipe.split_assignment: bucket = int(SHA256(UTF8('ess-stage2b-split-v1\0{dataset}\0{template_sha256}'))[:8], big-endian) mod 100; buckets 0..49=calibration, 50..99=heldout. Entire groups stay in one split; no split is reassigned after labels are opened.

selection_and_size.predicate_count_quota: Use bins [1],[2],[3-4],[5-7],[8-D] after removing empty bins. The schema-only planning rule makes d=1 descriptive (zero mandatory minimum), caps d=2 at the smaller of its equal-bin starting target and half the exact per-split schema capacity, and reallocates the deficits equally to bins with >=3 predicates. These are provisional planning targets only, not final immutable cohort quotas. Before any outcomes, run the fixed-attempt template pool against the complete historical fingerprint quarantine; only if every provisional bin/operator/graph target is met may the targets be frozen in the cohort manifest. Any shortfall blocks cohort freeze; no post-outcome reallocation is permitted.

schema_capacity_gate.supported_operator_rule: DatasetSpec numeric columns: =,<,<=,>,>=,[]; categorical columns: = only. This follows the pinned AreCEL categorical equality restriction; strict numeric < and > are an explicit prospective extension beyond its default range generator. Template tuples include column+operator+scalar/range class, not literal values.
schema_capacity_gate.enumeration: enumerate all 2^D column subsets (D<=13), count operator assignments analytically by family, classify exact available candidate graph and maximal-matching multiplicity by the pinned Issue #59 graph rule; enumerate actual template SHA split for all d=1 and d=2 templates. Emit exact upper bounds for every predicate-bin x operator-family x exclusive-graph-class intersection. This is schema-only and does not consult table rows, truth, estimates or traces.
schema_capacity_gate.quota_status: PROVISIONAL_SCHEMA_ONLY_TARGETS_NOT_FINAL; exact historical-quarantine and fixed-attempt pool evidence is a required pre-outcome gate
schema_capacity_gate.capacity_rule: For each operator family and exclusive graph class, schema upper bound <100 means STRUCTURALLY_INFEASIBLE and no 100-group minimum is imposed; upper bound >=100 makes it structurally eligible, but the actual fixed-attempt pool after complete historical quarantine must contain >=100 distinct templates in EACH split or cohort freeze is BLOCKED. The schema table is only a necessary upper bound; report all joint intersections, including zeros. No quota may be relaxed after outcomes.
schema_capacity_gate.implementation: schema_capacity.py; test_schema_capacity.py validates source pins, exact d=1/d=2 split capacities, d=1 descriptive status, >=50% d>=3 planning targets, d=2 headroom and global schema capacities. These tests do not establish a quarantined candidate-pool certificate.

selection_and_size.minimum_shape_coverage: in each split require >=500 queries with >=3 predicates; d=1 is descriptive only with no mandatory minimum. Require >=100 distinct templates per split for each operator family and exclusive graph class whose schema-only total upper bound is >=100. The mutually exclusive graph classes are 0 edges, 1 edge, >=2 disjoint edges, and conflict with >=2 maximal matchings. Conflict with exactly one maximal matching is structurally impossible for a graph containing a conflicting edge pair (the two conflicting edges each extend to distinct maximal matchings), and is explicitly reported with capacity zero rather than treated as an unmet quota. If a schema-feasible class lacks 100 templates in the fixed attempt pool after complete historical quarantine, mark BLOCKED; never drop it as 'infeasible' after observing pool shortfall.
selection_and_size.deterministic_acceptance: Generate at most 1000000 attempts; retain unique, non-quarantined template candidates with split, predicate-bin, operator-family and graph-class labels. Run this fixed-attempt generator only after assembling and hash-verifying the complete historical fingerprint quarantine. The provisional schema targets may be frozen unchanged only if the actual post-quarantine pool meets all split bin/operator/graph targets. If any target is unmet or any quarantine source is missing, mark BLOCKED before source-row literal generation or outcome access; do not reallocate after seeing outcomes. Candidate-priority ties use ascending SHA256('ess-stage2b-cohort-priority-v1\0{dataset}\0{seed}\0{template_sha256}'). The generator never consults truth/estimates and never changes the seed.
selection_and_size.query_id: issue64:{dataset}:{split}:{template_sha256}; literal values and exact-SQL SHA are separately recorded; the manifest maps each group to exactly one query ID
selection_and_size.manifest_freeze: write exclusive-create JSON manifest containing generator/source hashes, seeds, every accepted group/query ID, exact/template SHA, predicate/operator/graph strata, source table identity, scan/exclusion counts and split assignment; SHA256 it before opening test truth, EXPLAIN estimates, or PG traces
selection_and_size.implementation: experiments/pess-multidataset-heldout-stage2b/generalization-issue64/cohort_recipe.py implements and tests fingerprint, group/split ID and hash-counter primitives only; it is not a query builder and does not read any data. No complete historical fingerprint ledger or fixed-attempt pool certificate is currently available; both are explicit BLOCKED pre-outcome gates, and no final quota or query manifest exists.

primary.name: per-dataset P95 Q-error with one-row floor (Q1)
primary.formula: Q1(E,A)=max(E,A,1)/max(min(E,A),1), for finite E>=0 and A>=0
primary.formula_reference: metric_reference.py::q1 and natural_qerror; tested against synthetic zero/positive cases only
primary.quantile: for each query and policy compute z=round_half_even_50((ln(Q1_rep1)+ln(Q1_rep2))/2) using Decimal precision 80; exponentiate z. Report nearest-rank empirical P95, rank=ceil(0.95*n), separately per dataset/policy/budget. A PESS P95 minus Nominal P95 is not a paired-delta quantile and is not interpreted as one.
primary.contrast: paired query estimand delta_i=round_half_even_50((ln(Q1_PESS_rep1)-ln(Q1_Nominal_rep1)+ln(Q1_PESS_rep2)-ln(Q1_Nominal_rep2))/2), Decimal precision 80. Implemented by metric_reference.py::paired_log_q1_delta. Report mean delta_i, distribution, and sign counts separately from each policy's P95. Resample normalized template groups; query/group ratio is 1.
primary.pairwise_classification: Use the same recorded delta_i estimand: benefit iff delta_i<0; harm iff delta_i>0; tie iff delta_i==0 after predeclared 50-decimal-place half-even quantization, implemented by metric_reference.py::paired_classification. This is a computational tie rule, not a mathematical equality claim. Arithmetic-mean Q1 paired effects are sensitivity only.
primary.uncertainty: within each dataset, run 10000 stratified bootstrap replicates using the pinned SHA-counter PRNG and bootstrap seed 6501/6502/6503/6504 by dataset. Resample query groups with replacement within frozen predicate-count bins, preserving each bin's cohort count and using identical sampled group indices for Empty/Nominal/PESS. Report 2.5th/97.5th nearest-rank percentile intervals for each policy P95, the PESS-minus-Nominal P95 contrast, and mean paired delta. These are within-cohort descriptive intervals, not population guarantees.
primary.replicate_failure: a query is pair-complete only if both repetitions return valid estimates for Empty, Nominal and PESS. Any missing/invalid replication is counted as UNRESOLVED, never replaced or silently removed. Primary P95 and paired sign summaries are INCONCLUSIVE unless all 1000 frozen queries are pair-complete; any valid-subset statistic is labelled descriptive only.
primary.adaptation_note: Q1 is an explicit one-row floor adaptation, not exactly AreCEL's natural positive-domain Q-error

secondary: per-dataset P50/P99/Max Q1 with the same aggregation rule
natural AreCEL Q-error max(E,A)/min(E,A) on E>0 and A>0 only, with eligible n and coverage reported; zero/nonpositive cases are never silently folded into this subset

counts of exact-zero agreement (E=0,A=0), estimate-only zero, truth-only zero, and invalid/nonfinite/negative/missing values; invalid or missing is not Q1 and forces the primary completeness gate to INCONCLUSIVE
mean absolute positive pre-clamp log error on its explicitly defined positive domain, as continuity with the model metric; keep distinct from clamped/rounded Plan Rows
per-query PESS-vs-Nominal paired log-Q1 deltas and sign counts as defined above; optional arithmetic Q1 deltas are sensitivity only
Empty/Nominal/PESS outcomes reported separately for every dataset and budget; no pooled primary statistic

strata.predicate_count: nonempty bins [1],[2],[3-4],[5-7],[8-D], per dataset D; use exact schema-capacity-derived per-split counts in cohort_generation_recipe.selection_and_size.schema_capacity_gate.quota_by_dataset_split, not equal counts
operator_family: unsupported/other (must be zero; otherwise fail closed)
strata.rule: strata are descriptive and predeclared; never drop an unfavorable query because its syntactic graph, payload or trace differs from the model

postgresql_physical_evaluation.comparison: for each dataset/budget, evaluate Empty and each selected Nominal/PESS unordered set; deduplicate identical sets but retain policy labels; paired query IDs across all treatments
postgresql_physical_evaluation.same_conditions: same pinned PG 16.14 instrumented build/source+binary hashes, table bytes/schema/import, GUCs, statistics target, ANALYZE sampling protocol, query text, session settings and resource limits within a dataset; isolate each treatment database and use the frozen counterbalanced seeded treatment permutation
postgresql_physical_evaluation.sample_block_definition: one block = (dataset ID, prepared table SHA256, schema SHA256, PostgreSQL source/binary/build-flags SHA256, GUC+statistics-target SHA256, ANALYZE sample algorithm/version, replicate seed, sampled stable-row-ID-set SHA256). A block is matched only if these fields are byte-identical across Empty/Nominal/PESS database clones; treatment DDL/ANALYZE sequence and clone order are recorded separately.
postgresql_physical_evaluation.sample_gate: freeze two replicate seeds and the treatment-order schedule before runs; record sampled stable row IDs or an independently verifiable sample-manifest digest for every treatment. Exact sample-manifest SHA equality within replicate is required for a matched block. If PostgreSQL cannot expose/prove the same sample, the paired primary comparison is BLOCKED; do not relabel different samples as matched.
postgresql_physical_evaluation.treatment_order_and_analyze: For every isolated treatment clone: import the same byte-pinned table, set the same predeclared per-column/default/extended-statistics targets, create requested objects in ascending frozen candidate index, execute exactly one ANALYZE on the relation, then freeze the resulting sample/OID/payload manifest before querying. Do not ANALYZE again within that block. Calibration singleton clone order is ascending candidate ID. Held-out unique treatment-set clone order in replicate 0 is ascending SHA256('ess-stage2b-treatment-order-v1\0{dataset}\0{treatment_set_id}'); replicate 1 uses the exact reverse order. Record actual sequence and order seed.
postgresql_physical_evaluation.creation_order: create selected objects in frozen ascending candidate index; record object definition, catalog OID, creation order, payload presence/usable MCV contents and per-query selected OIDs/clause mapping
postgresql_physical_evaluation.coverage: separately classify syntactic candidate availability, usable MCV payload, selected-stat OID trace, claimed clause indexes and trace completeness; EXPLAIN rows alone do not prove selected objects. A missing/incomplete trace blocks mechanism/selection interpretation for that query, but does not invalidate its Q1 if the plan estimate and frozen-cohort truth are valid; retain it in primary query-error metrics and mark physical coverage unverified.
postgresql_physical_evaluation.mismatch: retain and report queries where actual PG behavior is outside the prescribed matching assumptions; do not reinterpret them as a matching or exclude them from overall Q-error
postgresql_physical_evaluation.failure_policy: missing payload or trace is a coverage/mechanism state, not an exclusion from valid Q1. A missing plan estimate, missing truth, nonfinite value, negative estimate or query execution failure is an invalid replicate; retain the query ID, count it UNRESOLVED, never retry or replace a count-query plan, and mark the dataset-budget primary comparison INCONCLUSIVE if any required replicate remains invalid. Only cluster/setup may retry once before the first plan. Every plan attempt consumes the query-plan cap.

prospective_caps.datasets: up to four; minimum two pass all gates for cross-dataset replication
prospective_caps.query_cap_derivation: Calibration: 4 datasets * exactly 1000 frozen calibration queries * exactly 1 query/group * at most (1 Empty + 10 singleton candidate) sets/dataset * exactly 1 calibration sample replicate = 44000 plan attempts. Held-out: 4 * exactly 1000 frozen queries * exactly 1 query/group * at most 7 deduplicated Empty/Nominal/PESS treatment sets/dataset * exactly 2 sample replicates = 56000. Total hard maximum = 100000 PostgreSQL estimate-plan attempts across both phases, including failures. No extra measured pilot, retry query or replacement query; setup-only retry may occur before any plan. If fewer datasets/sets are authorized, actual caps reduce using the same formula.
prospective_caps.wall_time_budget: proposed hard cap 24 elapsed hours per dataset including import, ANALYZE, query trace and reruns; confirm hardware feasibility before authorization
prospective_caps.disk_budget: proposed hard cap 100 GiB total disposable runtime data; confirm available capacity before authorization
prospective_caps.reruns: no count-query plan is retried; a cluster/setup failure may be retried once before any query plan, with attempt logged. Every EXPLAIN/count-query invocation, including a failed one, consumes the fixed cap. No outcome-driven reruns or replacement queries.
prospective_caps.stop: stop a dataset at first violated integrity/resource cap; mark BLOCKED/INCONCLUSIVE and do not expand scope
